records.text: Amanda Bakker testified that laboratory information indicated the backpack belonged to someone on Charlie Kirk's detail, although the communication log was not hers.
records.speaker: Amanda Bakker

appearances.snippet: Well Left behind by a bystander or according to your notes at page 20, the backpack belongs to Kirk's detainees. ... Yes, based on the individual that, that was not my communication log, that was someone else within the laboratory, that was the information that they received.

verification.notes: The embedded court footage records counsel referring to a laboratory note that the backpack belonged to someone on Kirk detail, followed by Bakker saying the communication log was not hers but that this was the information received by the laboratory. This verifies the narrowly attributed testimony and does not independently establish who owned the backpack.

records.text: Amanda Bakker testified that the FBI initially processed the backpack items for DNA, then learned the backpack might have been left by a bystander and made no comparisons.
records.speaker: Amanda Bakker

appearances.snippet: So initially we didn't have any information so we processed that. Those are items that are good for DNA. Not having any information from the investigators we process them for DNA. ... As the investigation continues, it was determined that that backpack was potentially left behind by a by a bystander and there was no comparisons needed at that time.

verification.notes: The embedded preliminary-hearing footage records FBI examiner Amanda Bakker saying the lab initially processed the backpack items for DNA because it had no investigative information, then learned the backpack may have been left by a bystander and that comparisons were not needed at that time. Current hearing coverage independently reports the bystander determination.
